# Configuration

Every knob the bots and the orchestrator read, in one place.

## Environment variables

Put them in `.env` (loaded by `node --env-file=.env …`, see `.env.example`) or export them; the orchestrator passes its environment to every bot it spawns.

<!-- env-table:start -->
*Generated by `scripts/gen_env_docs.js` from the `process.env` reads in `bots/` and `orchestrator/`; run `npm run docs` after adding one. `npm test` fails when this table is stale or a variable lacks a note.*

| Variable | Read by | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_COMPACT` | bot (`agent/model.js`) | on | `0` disables compaction (the API summarises the conversation, keeping the focus card, coordinates, people, inventory and furnace contents). Anthropic models only. |
| `AGENT_COMPACT_TOKENS` | bot (`agent/model.js`) | `120000` | Input-token count at which compaction triggers. |
| `AGENT_CONTEXT_EDIT` | bot (`agent/model.js`) | on | `0` disables API-side context editing (clearing old tool results once the context passes about 60k tokens). Anthropic models only. |
| `AGENT_EFFORT` | bot (`agent/model.js`) | `medium` | Thinking effort per turn: `low`, `medium` or `high`. On Gemini it becomes the thinking level unless `GEMINI_THINKING` overrides it. |
| `AGENT_EXIT_BEARING` | bot (`agent/tools/move.js`) | a stable hash of the bot name | Degrees (0 = north, 90 = east) that `leave_spawn` walks out on when the bot starts inside the spawn zone. The orchestrator sets one per bot, evenly spaced around its roster, so a fleet fans out; the tool's `direction` input overrides it. |
| `AGENT_MAX_TURNS` | bot (`agent/loop.js`) | `600` | Turn ceiling per session; the loop ends with reason `max_turns`. |
| `AGENT_MAX_USD` | bot (`agent/loop.js`) | `5` | Spend ceiling per bot session; the loop ends itself with reason `budget` when the running total reaches it. |
| `AGENT_MODEL` | bot + orchestrator (`agent/main.js`, `agent/model.js`, `agent/smoke_gemini.js`, `index.js`) | `LLM_MODEL`, else `claude-opus-5` | Model for the agent loop. A `gemini-*` id routes every turn through the Gemini adapter (`bots/agent/gemini.js`); anything else goes to the Anthropic SDK. Setting `GEMINI_API_KEY` alone does nothing: this variable decides. Also read by `smoke_gemini.js`. |
| `AGENT_STRATEGIST_EFFORT` | bot (`agent/main.js`) | `high` | Thinking effort for the strategist. |
| `AGENT_STRATEGIST_MODEL` | bot (`agent/main.js`) | `claude-opus-5` | Model behind the `think` tool (the strategist memo). May be a Gemini id. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | bot (`agent/model.js`) | — | Anthropic API key for every model turn when the model is a Claude model. Required unless `LLM_API_KEY` is set or every model is a Gemini one. |
| `FLEET_BUDGET_ACTION` | orchestrator (`args.js`) | `pause` | `kill` stops running bots when the ceiling is hit instead of only pausing new spawns (same as `--budget-action kill`). |
| `FLEET_MAX_USD_PER_DAY` | orchestrator (`args.js`) | — | Fleet spend ceiling per rolling 24 hours across every bot, same as `--budget`; the flag wins when both are given. |
| `FLEET_WEB_DEV` | orchestrator (`web.js`) | — | When set, the web dashboard re-reads `orchestrator/web/index.html` on every request instead of caching it (for editing the page). |
| `FLEET_WEB_PORT` | orchestrator (`web.js`) | `4545` | Port of the standalone web dashboard (`node orchestrator/web.js`); `--port` wins. The orchestrator takes `--web <port>` instead. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | bot (`agent/gemini.js`) | — | Google AI Studio key for the Gemini adapter. Required when `AGENT_MODEL` or `AGENT_STRATEGIST_MODEL` is a Gemini model. |
| `GEMINI_CONTEXT_CHARS` | bot (`agent/gemini.js`) | `400000` | Size of the Gemini history (in characters, about 100k tokens) at which the adapter blanks tool results older than the newest 30 and re-shows the focus card, since Gemini has no server-side context editing. |
| `GEMINI_THINKING` | bot (`agent/gemini.js`) | from `AGENT_EFFORT` | Gemini thinking level: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `off`. If the API rejects the field the adapter retries without it and logs `gemini_thinking_config_rejected`. |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | bot (`agent/gemini.js`) | — | Alternative name for `GEMINI_API_KEY`. |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | bot (`agent/model.js`) | — | Alternative name for the Anthropic key; takes precedence over `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. |
| `LLM_MODEL` | bot + orchestrator (`agent/main.js`, `agent/model.js`, `index.js`) | — | Older name for `AGENT_MODEL`, used only when `AGENT_MODEL` is unset. An old `.env` that sets `LLM_MODEL` to a Claude model keeps the bots on Claude however many Gemini keys it also holds. |
| `MC_SERVER_DIR` | bot (`agent/main.js`) | `<repo>/server` | The Paper server folder the bots read at boot: WorldGuard regions and the Factions board (protection zones), Essentials `worth.yml` (sell prices) and `mstore/factions_mconf/instance.json` (faction rules). See [server.md](server.md). |
| `REDIS_HOST` | orchestrator (`index.js`) | `localhost` | Redis host for the orchestrator's chat feed. Each bot reads its own Redis host from its profile (`redis.host`), not from this variable. |
| `REDIS_PORT` | orchestrator (`index.js`) | `6379` | Redis port for the orchestrator's chat feed (bots: profile `redis.port`). |
<!-- env-table:end -->

Precedence, highest first: a command-line flag (orchestrator), then the
environment, then the profile file, then the default in the code. The
orchestrator passes its whole environment to every bot it spawns, so a
variable exported before `npm run fleet` reaches every bot; per-bot
differences go in the profile.

Two things are not environment variables on purpose: the Redis host and
port a *bot* uses come from its profile (`redis.host`, `redis.port`), and
the model key is never read from a profile.

## Profiles (`bots/profiles/<name>.yaml`)

`bots/core/profileLoader.js` reads the file named by the stem you pass
(`test_bot_oss`) or, failing that, the file whose `username:` matches. It
returns exactly these fields; anything else in the file is ignored.

| Field | Type, default | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `username` | string, **required** | the Minecraft login name; logs, transcript and database file names |
| `archetype` | `pvper`, `builder`, `farmer`, `grinder`, `ratter`, `diplomat`; default `generic` | the system prompt, blueprint selection, the scheduler tally in `orchestrator/test_orchestrator.js` |
| `skill_tier` | integer, default 1 | the system prompt; blueprint tiers (`tier_min`) |
| `ambition` | number 0–1, default 0.5 | the system prompt (drive to found a faction rather than join one) |
| `faction_preferences` | object (`style`, `themes[]`), default `{}` | the system prompt's faction naming hint |
| `backstory` | string, default empty | the system prompt |
| `values` | object of 0–1 numbers (`risk_tolerance`, `social_preference`, `material_greed`, `loyalty`, `curiosity`), default `{}` | the system prompt |
| `voice` | object (`tone`, `greeting`, `catchphrases[]`, `typo_rate`, `caps_when_tilted`, `signature_rate`, `punctuation`, `ambient_frequency`), default `{}` | the system prompt and `bots/social/voiceFilter.js`, which rewrites everything `say` sends |
| `host`, `port`, `version`, `auth` | `localhost`, `25565`, `"1.8.9"`, `offline` | `bots/core/bot.js` (mineflayer login) |
| `redis.host`, `redis.port`, `redis.password`, `redis.db` | `localhost`, `6379`, none, `0` | `bots/core/eventBus.js` |
| `redis.channels.events`, `.commands`, `.responses` | `mc:events`, `mc:commands`, `mc:responses` | `eventBus.js`; must match `server/plugins/BotBridge/config.yml` |
| `spawn` | `{x, y, z}`, default `{0, 64, 0}` | only a fallback for `goto named: spawn` before the bot has seen the real spawn point |
| `combat` | object (`reaction_ms_min/max`, `aim_error_deg`, `cps`, `block_hit_rate`, `pot_at_hp`, `pot_success_rate`, `combo_follow_rate`, `flee_at_hp`, `preferred_weapon`, `aim_lag_ms`), default `{}` | `bots/world/combat.js` |
| `schedule.primary_hours`, `.secondary_hours` | `[from, to]` hours, default `[18, 23]` and `[14, 18]` | `orchestrator/scheduler.js` |
| `schedule.session_minutes` | `[min, max]`, default `[30, 120]` | `orchestrator/spawner.js` (SIGTERM at the end of the window); `--session` overrides it |
| `schedule.weekend_boost` | boolean, default `true` | `scheduler.js` |
| `schedule.always_online` | boolean, default `false` | `scheduler.js` (`--only` sets it for the roster) |

The characters and what each field does to play are described in
[profiles.md](profiles.md).

## Server files

`MC_SERVER_DIR` points at the Paper folder; the bots read three files from
it at boot and fall back to shipped defaults when they are missing. Which
files and what happens without them: [server.md](server.md).

## The data folder

Everything a bot or the orchestrator writes goes under `data/` (git-ignored,
created on demand):

| Path | What | Safe to delete? |
|---|---|---|
| `data/bots/<name>.db` | SQLite: events the bot observed, key-value state (faction state, home, focus card) | yes; the bot forgets its home, focus and faction state |
| `data/sessions/<name>/<start>.jsonl` | one transcript per session | yes; the dashboards lose history |
| `data/memory/<name>/*.md` | the memory tool's files (journal, plans, places, people) | yes; the bot forgets across sessions |
| `data/skills/` | model-written skills shared by every bot, with `index.json` | yes; saved skills are gone |
| `data/logs/` | `<name>.log` per bot, `orchestrator.log` | yes |
| `data/fleet_status.json` | the orchestrator's last dashboard snapshot | yes |
| `data/diagnostics/` | left over from the retired planner stack; nothing writes it | yes |

Formats and what each process reads: [data-and-storage.md](data-and-storage.md).
